_comment: Answer key for C1 extraction against scene_fixture.json.
Derived from the planted elements annotated in api/scripts/make_test_pdf.py.
This scores EXTRACTION only — did we find the right things, in the right
element, in the right category. Risk ratings are B7's ground-truth.md and
`canonical_match` is a lowercase substring that must appear in the produced
canonical_name. Exact canonical strings are C3's business (normalisation);
C1 only has to identify the same real-world thing.

expected_present.note: Song specified to play on screen. The RED case in C6 — sync + master.
Can with logo facing the lens. Depiction, not mention.
Record label mark legible on the vinyl label.
Hopper died 1967 — inside the life+70 term. Shown on screen.
THE SPLIT. Same song as el_2, dialogue reference only. Must be a separate record with element_type=dialogue, or the product's core distinction is lost.
Real restaurant, identifiable on screen — trade dress.
Same mark as el_10, in dialogue and neutral — a business conversation, not a product claim. B7's gt_04, GREEN. The disparaging case is el_50.
Second mark in the same line.
Quoted Shakespeare — public domain, but must still be found. Accepts a shakespeare canonical too; see canonical_alt.
Described in an action line as the actual music industry executive.
Picasso died 1973 — estate holds until 2044. Shown on screen.
Second depiction, scene 6. A bottle on a table with no framing direction — the low-prominence end of the same category as el_10.
'Coke'. Tests that a nickname resolves to the same canonical entity as 'Coca-Cola' — which is the entire reason canonical names exist.
The brand attacked in dialogue with a health claim. B7's gt_05, RED. The hardest case in the document; without this pin, losing it is silent.
A living public figure named in dialogue. B7's gt_14, AMBER.

expected_absent.why: The precision trap. A fictional character in this script who happens to carry a plausible real name. Extracting him as a real person is a false positive.

acceptable_extra.why: Nielsen is a real company named in el_5 and el_16. Defensible either way — reported, not penalised.
Edward Hopper as a person alongside the artwork record.
Pablo Picasso as a person alongside the artwork record.
The band as a separate music/person record alongside the song.
Marcus Harman also named in dialogue at el_16 and el_19.
The author alongside the quoted line at el_25.
Nobu also named in dialogue at el_43 — a second mention, correctly kept separate.
The can's logo categorised as `logo` as well as `trademark`. Overlapping categories on one depiction are defensible; C3 collapses them.
Named twice, el_55 and el_57, both dialogue. C3 groups them into one research task; C6 still rates each mention.
